info.title: Ratatoss controller control protocol
info.description: HTTPS, UTF-8 JSON. Retry network failures, 429 and 5xx with jittered 1–30 second backoff and honor Retry-After. Display consent and permission failures. Never log credentials or codes.

post.summary: Enroll a device with a one-time code
post.description: Use an administrator-issued 256-bit code, with a 10-minute TTL. Consume the code atomically when issuing the device token. This endpoint has no bearer or idempotency key. If the response is lost after consumption, an operator must revoke the orphaned device/token before issuing a replacement code.

post.summary: Open a pairing session as an enrolled device
post.description: Issue a one-time 128-bit pairing code with a 10-minute TTL. Share it out of band. On identical replay while the unclaimed code is still usable, return the original code and deadline. Once claimed or expired, omit the secret by returning the applicable conflict or expiry error. Scope the key to device, method and concrete route. Store the payload digest and committed result while the linked job or pair exists; return 409 on a different payload for the same key. The request has no body.

get.summary: List the caller’s pairing sessions and peers
get.description: Only show sessions involving the caller. Pending comparison uses the same six-digit string on both devices, including leading zeros. Active pairs expose the counterpart device ID for selection as a job target. Connection state is independent of the pair state.

post.summary: Claim a session as a different enrolled device
post.description: Atomically consume a valid pairing code. No authority is granted until both parties confirm. Check the idempotency record before rejecting reuse of the code. Self-pairing is prohibited. Scope the key to device, method and concrete route. Store the payload digest and committed result while the linked job or pair exists; return 409 on a different payload for the same key.

post.summary: Confirm or reject a claimed pair as a participant
post.description: Compare the six-digit code out of band before confirming. Both parties must confirm before the deadline. Any rejection terminates the session. At most one ACTIVE pair may exist for an unordered device pair. Scope the key to device, method and concrete route. Store the payload digest and committed result while the linked job or pair exists; return 409 on a different payload for the same key.

delete.summary: Unpair as an active pair participant
delete.description: Block new offers and revoke pending offers atomically. Previously accepted offers continue subject to their own withdrawal controls. Scope the key to device, method and concrete route. Store the payload digest and committed result while the linked job or pair exists; return 409 on a different payload for the same key. The request has no body.

post.summary: Create a job as the file source
post.description: Register the source’s durably stored immutable manifest and one pending offer per distinct ACTIVE paired target. Validate all targets, configured manifest limits and layout before committing. Compute the canonical digest and set the offer TTL from commit (default 24 hours). Scope the key to device, method and concrete route. Store the payload digest and committed result while the linked job or pair exists; return 409 on a different payload for the same key.

get.summary: List offers addressed to the caller
get.description: The list includes pending and terminal states. Each record contains source name, file name, size and deadline.

get.summary: Read a detailed offer as its target
get.description: Obtain the canonical manifest and digest for local storage preparation and consent.

post.summary: Accept or decline an offer as its target
post.description: A decision applies to PENDING before expiry. Before ACCEPT, persist local consent and the destination, and supply the matching canonical digest and explicit permission to forward. The local destination path stays on the node. Scope the key to device, method and concrete route. Store the payload digest and committed result while the linked job or pair exists; return 409 on a different payload for the same key.

post.summary: Withdraw an accepted unfinished offer as its target
post.description: Block future scheduling and cancel live assignments for this participant at both endpoints (RX or TX). Scope the key to device, method and concrete route. Store the payload digest and committed result while the linked job or pair exists; return 409 on a different payload for the same key. The request has no body.

post.summary: Cancel an open job as its original source
post.description: Revoke pending offers, cancel unfinished accepted offers and stop assignments. Preserve all previously committed receipts. Scope the key to device, method and concrete route. Store the payload digest and committed result while the linked job or pair exists; return 409 on a different payload for the same key. The request has no body.

get.summary: Read the job as its source or addressed target
get.description: The SOURCE view contains all destinations; TARGET contains only the caller’s offer and required job metadata. OPEN persists while an accepted target is offline. After all offers are terminal, COMPLETE means every target has a receipt, PARTIAL means some do, and NO_DELIVERY means none do. CANCELED is explicit source termination. Verified bytes count only registered verified batches.

post.summary: Report current boot and available slots as the caller
post.description: Send every five seconds. After 20 seconds without heartbeat mark the device offline and invalidate its assignments. A changed boot or offline reconnect requires reconciliation before scheduling. Heartbeats are transient and use no idempotency key; send a fresh snapshot on retry.

post.summary: Replace verified availability as source or consenting target
post.description: Validate boot against the current heartbeat and range-check batch IDs; atomically replace the caller’s full verified inventory. Clear removed availability before replaying ACKs. Serialize snapshots and outbox per job, discard pending ACKs for lost or corrupt batches, and reject stale boot snapshots. Scope the key to device, method and concrete route. Store the payload digest and committed result while the linked job or pair exists; return 409 on a different payload for the same key.

get.summary: Poll the caller’s complete assignment snapshot
get.description: Poll every second while working or with free slots. Only live OFFERED or RUNNING leases involving the caller appear. Omission invalidates local work. OFFERED never contains a code. RUNNING TX includes its code so the sender can start. RUNNING RX uses the code already returned by ready. Default prepare/run leases are 30/180 seconds, configurable; use the shorter adapter or monotonic lease deadline.

post.summary: Reserve the staging and slot as the assigned RX
post.description: Transition OFFERED to RUNNING and return the Croc code, enabling the same code in the next TX poll. A matching replay returns the same code only while the lease is live and reports the remaining duration at replay time; it never renews the lease. Expired leases return 410. Scope the key to device, method and concrete route. Store the payload digest and committed result while the linked job or pair exists; return 409 on a different payload for the same key. The request has no body.

post.summary: Acknowledge a durably verified batch as its assigned RX
post.description: Verify the batch digest and consent. If the lease is still live, mark that attempt successful and record availability atomically. An otherwise valid late ACK may record availability while participation is authorized, without changing the terminal attempt. Cancel a redundant replacement independently. Replay of an already processed ACK returns its prior result without restoring availability removed by reconcile. Scope the key to device, method and concrete route. Store the payload digest and committed result while the linked job or pair exists; return 409 on a different payload for the same key.

post.summary: Report assignment failure as either assigned endpoint
post.description: Validate the live attempt before ending it and releasing slots. Report structured failures without local paths or secrets. Scope the key to device, method and concrete route. Store the payload digest and committed result while the linked job or pair exists; return 409 on a different payload for the same key.

post.summary: Record a verified final delivery as its consenting target
post.description: Submit only after verifying and durably publishing the final file. Check all values against the manifest and require all batches in the caller’s registry. Record one immutable receipt per job and target. Scope the key to device, method and concrete route. Store the payload digest and committed result while the linked job or pair exists; return 409 on a different payload for the same key.

CrocCode.description: Opaque session secret. Only deliver to the assigned endpoints as described.

Manifest.description: Validate configured limits and canonical digest outside JSON Schema. Arrays use zero-based consecutive indices and contiguous offsets and each covers exactly size bytes. All segments except the last use the full respective span. batch_size is a multiple of piece_size. Zero size means empty arrays and the SHA-256 of zero bytes. Reject duplicate keys, Unicode surrogates, and non-integer numeric tokens; preserve name code points and calculate manifest_sha256 on sorted-key compact UTF-8 without BOM or newline.

BadRequest.description: Malformed or invalid request, including a missing or malformed idempotency key when required.

Unauthorized.description: Missing, invalid or revoked device credential.

NotFound.description: Resource does not exist or is outside the caller scope. Enrollment and claim codes that are invalid, expired or consumed have the same generic failure within each operation.

Conflict.description: Lifecycle, consent, integrity or idempotency conflict.

error.message: Idempotency key was already used with a different payload.

Retry-After.description: Seconds or an HTTP date. Honor this value when present.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Agent-generated UUID. Keep the same key and payload on retries.
